The first recorded computer "bug" was a real moth, taped into a Harvard logbook in 1947.
The computer that flew Apollo 11 to the Moon had about 4 KB of RAM. This README is bigger.
Python is named after Monty Python, not the snake.
JavaScript was written in 10 days in 1995. It shows, and it runs the world anyway.
The first domain name ever registered was symbolics.com, on 15 March 1985.
"Wi-Fi" doesn't stand for anything. It's a brand name that sounded like hi-fi.
The first computer mouse, built in 1964, was a block of wood with two metal wheels.
The first webcam, set up in 1991, watched a coffee pot so researchers could skip pointless trips.
CAPTCHA stands for Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart.
Email (1971) is 18 years older than the World Wide Web (1989).
The @ in email addresses was picked in 1971 because it was the one key nobody used in names.
Ada Lovelace published the first computer program in 1843, for a machine that was never finished.
ENIAC, one of the first electronic computers, weighed about 27 tonnes and filled a room.
On 19 January 2038, 32-bit Unix clocks run out of seconds and roll over. Mark your calendar.
Old games cap stats at 255 because one byte can only count from 0 to 255.
Early arcade cabinets kept high scores in RAM, so unplugging the machine wiped the leaderboard.
The word "robot" comes from the Czech "robota", meaning forced labour. It debuted in a 1920 play.
The save icon is a 3.5-inch floppy disk. It held 1.44 MB, less than one phone photo.
Half a byte is officially called a nibble.
The term "artificial intelligence" was coined for a 1956 summer workshop that planned to mostly solve it in two months.
The first 1 GB hard drive shipped in 1980, weighed about 250 kg and cost more than a house.
Linus Torvalds started writing Git in April 2005. Within days it was tracking its own source code.
The QWERTY layout dates from 1870s typewriters. Your keyboard is older than the light bulb.
"Rubber duck debugging" is real advice from a 1999 book: explain your code to a duck, find the bug yourself.
